response_draft.draft_text: For a standard self-service customer, official Ola Maps docs say the API pricing and payment changes take effect on 1 September 2026 and apply to all customers on standard self-service platform plans, including those currently using automatic card payments. Docs say to add credits from 1 September 2026; the credit balance may become negative without service interruption during the grace period, and credits should be added before 8 September 2026 and kept sufficient for expected usage beyond the free tier. After 8 September the grace period ends; maintaining a sufficient credit balance for usage beyond the free tier is documented as helping to keep API access uninterrupted. Do not invent a hard Autocomplete cutoff or an automatic suspension date — that is not stated. Instructions for adding credits will be shared soon, so a human should track that follow-up. If there are questions about expected charges, adding credits, or the impact on the account, official docs say the Ola Maps team will assist throughout the transition — hand those account-specific questions to a human.

Ola Maps' official OpenAPI documents GET /places/v1/reverse-geocode with a required latlng query parameter described as the coordinates to reverse geocode, and the published example is a single coordinate pair; the same spec lists no batch reverse-geocode path. response_draft.draft_text: Call the Geocoding API v6 reverse endpoint with `longitude`, `latitude` and a valid access token. To request address features only, add `types=address`. Note that Mapbox's example filters the returned features by type; it does not promise an address result where no address feature is available.

response_draft.draft_text: Use the reverse endpoint with the `types=address` filter to ask for address features. Mapbox documents that reverse geocoding can return features at multiple administrative levels, and its default is at most one feature at each level (for example, address, region and country). The docs do not guarantee that an address feature exists for every coordinate, so verify the returned feature types rather than assuming a missing address is an API fault.

citations.span: The reverse geocoding query type allows you to look up a pair of coordinates and returns the geographic features there, including a standardized address or place and full geographic context.
The default behavior in reverse geocoding is to return at most one feature at each of the multiple levels of the administrative hierarchy (for example, one address, one region, one country).
$curl "https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/reverse?longitude=-73.989&latitude=40.733&types=address&access_token=YOUR_MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN"
